title: Test probes execute the target file directly instead of running it under the test runner

finding.claim: Test probes execute the target file directly instead of running it under the test runner
finding.evidence: For kind 'test', the harness builds argv as the Python interpreter plus the target path, so a documented spec like {'kind': 'test', 'target': 'tests/test_x.py'} is executed as a script rather than through unittest/pytest semantics. That breaks common test targets that rely on discovery, fixtures, or package-relative imports, causing reachable false failures for supported probe requests.
finding.recommendation: Invoke an actual test runner for 'test' probes, for example 'python -m unittest <target>' or a project-defined runner, and validate the target format accordingly. If direct script execution is intended, rename the probe kind or documentation so callers do not expect test-runner behavior.

refutation.reason: The code explicitly constructs argv as [sys.executable, target] for test kind, which runs the target as a script via the Python interpreter rather than invoking a test runner. This matches the finding's description that the harness executes the target directly, confirming the defect.

probe.summary: Re-raise of the shadow set's 4cf81c69d7cf (ratified sustain_finding by the owner, 2026-11-04). The fix predates this workup: c3c1463 runs kind-'test' probes through the unittest runner and treats zero executed tests as an error, never a verdict. Verified at HEAD by the sandbox probe (`probes/closingB_probe_sandbox.py`, section 3): an unguarded FAILING test file now probes outcome='fail' (Ran 1 test, FAILED) — direct script execution would have run 0 tests and exited 0. The dedicated after-state probe (469e36e) covers the guarded/unguarded pair.
